# wallix-bastion_cluster (Data Source)

Get information on a global cluster resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific cluster
data "wallix-bastion_cluster" "web_cluster" {
  cluster_name = "web-servers"
}

# Use the cluster as the target of an application
resource "wallix-bastion_application" "web_app" {
  application_name  = "web-application"
  connection_policy = "RDP"
  target            = data.wallix-bastion_cluster.web_cluster.cluster_name

  paths {
    target      = "Interactive@web01:RDP"
    program     = "application_path"
    working_dir = "directory"
  }
}

# Inspect the cluster's membership
output "web_cluster_info" {
  value = {
    description         = data.wallix-bastion_cluster.web_cluster.description
    accounts            = data.wallix-bastion_cluster.web_cluster.accounts
    account_mappings     = data.wallix-bastion_cluster.web_cluster.account_mappings
    interactive_logins   = data.wallix-bastion_cluster.web_cluster.interactive_logins
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_name` (String)

### Read-Only

- `account_mappings` (Set of String)
- `accounts` (Set of String)
- `description` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `interactive_logins` (Set of String)

## Usage Notes

### Lookup Key

- **cluster_name**: The name of the cluster to look up. Returns an error if no cluster with this name exists.

### Returned Attributes

- **description**: Description of the cluster
- **accounts**: Set of `account@domain@device:service` entries granting direct account access to cluster members
- **account_mappings**: Set of `device:service` entries granting mapped account access to cluster members
- **interactive_logins**: Set of `device:service` entries granting direct interactive access to cluster members

A cluster typically populates at least one of `accounts`, `account_mappings`, or `interactive_logins`, depending on how the underlying resource was configured.

### Usage in Resources

The cluster name can be used as the `target` of a `wallix-bastion_application`, since the Bastion load-balances sessions across the cluster's members and automatically bypasses failed targets. A cluster isn't a device: `wallix-bastion_targetgroup` can't reference it in `device` (`Device '<cluster_name>' not found`); target groups reach it through the application.
